title: Around the home
subtitle: a spare room, a dishwasher, a duvet, curtains or blinds
summary: Name the rooms of a home and the things you find in the kitchen, the living room and the bedroom.

lesson.heading: Different homes
lesson.text: A **one-bedroom flat** has one bedroom. If two people **share** a room, they use it at the same time. A room that is your **own** is only for you. A **spare room** is a room you keep for guests, and a **study** is a room where people can work.

examples.text: When we first got married, we lived in a **one-bedroom flat**.
When our first child was born, she had to **share** our bedroom.
Our two teenage children have their **own** rooms.
We have a **spare room** for guests, and another bathroom.
My mum works at home, so she spends all day in the **study** on the computer.

lesson.heading: Rooms in a house
rows: where you sit, talk and watch TV
a room where people can work
a bedroom you keep for guests
a bathroom connected to a bedroom
a small room where you keep the washing machine

lesson.heading: In the kitchen
lesson.text: The **cooker** is where you cook, and it has one or two **ovens**. A **fridge** keeps food cool and a **freezer** keeps it frozen; a **fridge-freezer** does both. A **dishwasher** is a machine for washing dishes, and a **microwave** heats food very quickly.

examples.text: We've got a lovely big kitchen with a **fridge-freezer**, a **cooker** with two **ovens** and a **dishwasher**.
Next to it, there's a small **utility room** where we keep the **washing machine**.
Dad, there's no water coming out of the **tap** in the kitchen **sink**.
I'll put the **kettle** on and make some tea.
The clean cups and saucers are in that **cupboard**.

lesson.heading: sink or washbasin?
lesson.text: We usually talk about a **sink** in the kitchen, but a **(wash)basin** in the bathroom. **Tiles** are the flat squares on a wall or floor, most often in the kitchen or the bathroom.

examples.text: The dirty saucepans are in the kitchen **sink**.
I washed my hands in the **washbasin**.
The bathroom floor is covered in white **tiles**.

lesson.heading: In the living room
lesson.text: Some people like big soft **sofas** with lots of **cushions**; other people like **firm** **armchairs**. **Firm** is the opposite of **soft**. A **carpet** covers the whole floor; a **rug** is small and covers only part of a **wooden floor**.

examples.text: We used to have a **wooden** floor, but it was a bit noisy, so we put down a **carpet**.
I prefer a wooden floor with a **rug** in front of the fire.
There are three **cushions** on that big soft **sofa**.

lesson.heading: Two choices for the window and the bed

left.label: Curtains or blinds?
left.text: A **choice** is when you decide between two or more possibilities.
examples: When I got my new bedroom, my mum gave me a **choice** of **curtains** or **blinds**.
I'm happy with **curtains** or **blinds**; I really don't mind.

right.label: A duvet, or a sheet and a blanket?
right.text: You also choose one **pillow** or two for your head.
examples: Some people like a **sheet** and a **blanket**, but I prefer a **duvet**.
I can't sleep with only one **pillow**.

lesson.text: Careful with machines: a washing machine washes clothes, but a dishwasher washes plates and cups.

exercises.prompt: Which room do you usually find each thing in?
We used to have a ___ floor, but it was a bit noisy so we put down a carpet.
exercises.explanation: A wooden floor is often covered with a rug.

exercises.prompt: When I got my new bedroom, my mum gave me a ___ of curtains or blinds.
exercises.explanation: A choice is when you decide between two or more possibilities.

exercises.prompt: My mum works at home, so she spends all day in the ___ on the computer.
exercises.explanation: A study is a room in a house where people work.

exercises.prompt: As a child I had to ___ a room with my sister, but now I've got my own bedroom.
exercises.hint: (use it at the same time as someone else)
exercises.explanation: Share = use something at the same time as someone else.

exercises.prompt: We often have guests to stay, but fortunately we've got a ___ room.
exercises.explanation: A spare room is a bedroom you keep for guests.

exercises.prompt: Dad, there's no water coming out of the ___ in the kitchen sink.
exercises.explanation: You turn on the tap and the water runs into the sink.

exercises.prompt: Our kitchen is small, but we have a ___ room for the washing machine.
exercises.explanation: A utility room is a small room for the washing machine and other machines.

exercises.prompt: Some people like a sheet and a blanket, but I prefer a ___.
exercises.explanation: A duvet is the thick soft cover you use instead of a sheet and blankets.

exercises.prompt: There's a family bathroom, but I've got my own ___ shower room next to the bedroom.
exercises.explanation: An en-suite bathroom or shower room is connected to the bedroom.

exercises.statement: We usually talk about a sink in the kitchen, but a washbasin in the bathroom.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Both are for water, but they have different names.

exercises.statement: A rug covers the whole floor of a room.
exercises.explanation: A carpet covers the whole floor. A rug is small and covers only part of it.
